Legim Nan Diri (Haitian Vegetable Stew with Rice)

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6-8Prep 45 minCook 1 hour 30 min

This hearty and flavorful vegetable stew, "Legim Nan Diri," is a staple of Haitian cuisine, often served mixed with or alongside rice. For the Fete de Papa Zaka, the benevolent farmer Loa, this dish is a perfect offering, symbolizing the bounty of the harvest and the earth's generosity, aligning with Zaka's domain of agriculture and sustenance.

Ingredients

  • 1 large eggplant (about 1.5 lb / 680 g), peeled and diced
  • 1/2 small head of green cabbage (about 1 lb / 450 g), cored and roughly chopped
  • 2 carrots (about 8 oz / 225 g), peeled and sliced
  • 1 green bell pepper, cored and diced
  • 1 red bell pepper, cored and diced
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) chopped fresh parsley
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) chopped scallions (green onions)
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) vegetable oil, divided
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) tomato paste
  • 1 sprig fresh thyme (or 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme)
  • 1 scotch bonnet pepper (optional, whole, pierced a few times)
  • 4 cups (960 ml) vegetable broth or water
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
  • Optional: 1 lb (450 g) beef stew meat or smoked pork, cut into small pieces
  • 2 cups (400 g) long-grain white rice, rinsed
  • 3 cups (720 ml) water (for rice)
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) salt (for rice)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) vegetable oil (for rice)

Method

  1. Prepare the Legim vegetables: Peel and dice the eggplant, chop the cabbage, slice the carrots, dice the bell peppers, chop the onion, mince the garlic, chop parsley and scallions.
  2. If using meat: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of the vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Brown the meat on all sides, then remove and set aside.
  3. In the same pot, add the remaining 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of oil (if needed). Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic, chopped parsley, and chopped scallions and cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
  4. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens slightly.
  5. Add the diced eggplant, chopped cabbage, sliced carrots, green and red bell peppers, and fresh thyme sprig (and the whole scotch bonnet pepper, if using). If using meat, return it to the pot.
  6. Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Season with 1 teaspoon (5 g) salt and 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for at least 1 hour, or until all vegetables are very tender and the stew has thickened. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. The vegetables should break down and create a rich sauce.
  7. While the Legim is simmering, prepare the Diri: In a separate medium pot, combine the rinsed rice, 3 cups (720 ml) water, 1 teaspoon (5 g) salt, and 1 tablespoon (15 ml) vegetable oil. Bring to a boil over high heat.
  8. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the water is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
  9. Once the Legim is done, remove the thyme sprig and scotch bonnet pepper (if used). Taste and adjust seasoning.
  10. To serve, either mix the Legim directly into the cooked rice in the pot, or serve generous portions of Legim over individual servings of rice.

Tips

  • The longer the Legim simmers, the more the vegetables break down and meld, creating a richer, thicker stew. Don't rush it!
  • For a vegetarian version, simply omit the meat. The dish is incredibly flavorful and satisfying on its own.
  • For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a bay leaf to the Legim stew while it simmers.
